newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries close steady amid qrtly refunding.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries close steady amid qrtly refunding.

text.p: The prices of U.S. Treasury securities closed higher Wednesday as the bond market remained in a fairly tight range before the final leg of the Treasury's quarterly refunding operation.

The Treasury sold $12 billion of 10-year issues at an average yield of 6.205 percent on Wednesday, with another sale of 30-year bonds slated for Thursday. The Treasury's three-year auction produced average yields of 6.04 percent on Tuesday, slightly higher than anticipated by many market participants.
There was little economic data available to trade upon. The Federal Reserve's Beige Book showing moderate price increases and tighter labor markets, but "scattered" wage pressures.
Prices deteriorated after the auction results were announced, but for no good reason, said Roseanne Cahn, economist at Credit Suisse First Boston.
Christopher Low, senior economist at HSBC Markets Inc, said the fact the market has held in so well during the current supply deluge was positive.
"With the refunding ending (on Thursday) we could see either see relief or difficulty in digesting" results, Low said.
The next significant numbers for the bond market would not be seen until next Wednesday when retail sales and producer prices data were due, Low said.

He said that at current levels growth could be expected to rise as much as 3.0 to 3.5 percent in the third quarter, putting the Federal Reserve in the position of having to again seriously consider tightening monetary policy at its policy-making meetings in September or November.

GovPX reported that by 1500 EDT/1900 GMT trading volume was four percent below average for a Wednesday from the third quarter of last year as bill volume was 41 percent below average and coupon volume 19 percent above average.
The Treasury's second leg of its quarterly refunding operation met with soft results, with the 10-year average yield at 6.205 percent with a tail out to 6.218 percent.
The Federal Reserve refrained from entering the banking system on Wednesday, surprising some analysts who had projected an add need of us much as $6 billion a day in the current maintenance period.
The Treasury's 30-year bond was closing 4/32 higher at 101-28/32 to yield 6.48 percent.
The 10-year issue was at 102-30/32, up 4/32 to yield 6.22 percent. The five-year issue was up 3/32 at 99-18/32 to yield 6.10 percent. The two-year was 1/32 higher at 99-30/32 to yield 5.91 percent.

At the short end of the maturity spectrum, the three-month bill rate was unchanged at 5.15 percent and the six-month down one basis point at 5.20 percent. The year bill was down two basis points at 5.22 percent.
